title: Kernel Heuristic Harvester — Sequence/Arch Adaptor for Warmstart Kernel Picks
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Our current kernel-picker relies on static heuristics that degrade across heterogeneous hardware and varying sequence-length distributions. Prefill workloads often prefer compute-dense kernels with higher occupancy while decode favors low-latency kernels; current routing flips cause tail latency spikes and inefficient GPU utilization.

Goal: Build a lightweight, production-safe "heuristic harvester" that continuously collects compact per-request signatures (architecture, effective seq_len, token-phase, batch size, KV footprint, attention mode), runs microprobes for candidate kernels with controlled budget, and synthesizes a warmstart mapping that is indexed by (instance-arch, model-family, seq_len-bucket, phase). The harvester should seed the runtime's kernel selector with high-confidence choices and retain a small bandit-style explorer to adapt to distribution drift.

Design highlights:
- Compact signature: 64-bit fingerprint combining arch hash, seq_len bucket, avg token-phase, and recent latency percentiles.
- Microprobe flow: when a low-confidence signature is observed, the agent schedules a background microprobe (1-2 requests) that runs alternative kernels instrumented for latency/occupancy and KV behavior; probes are rate-limited and throttled to avoid SLO impact.
- Cost model: probes emit token-cost vs latency metrics; harvester aggregates into a sparse cost surface and computes a utility score (latency SLO penalty + token-cost) for each kernel candidate.
- Warmstart map: persistent LRU-backed mapping stored per-node and pushed to control plane for cross-node warmstarts; entries carry confidence, last-observed, and rollback-safe fallback kernel.
- Phase-aware selection: split policy for prefill vs decode; prefill favors throughput-optimized kernels and KV-friendly implementations, decode prioritizes low tail-latency kernels and smaller memory footprints.
- Safety: any candidate kernel that increases 99p latency by >10% triggers automatic rollback and blacklisting for that signature for a cooldown period.
- Observability: new dashboard slices for signature coverage, probe frequency, warmstart accuracy, and cost/latency trade-offs.

Why different from prior work: Instead of full Bayesian optimization or heavy online profiling, this is a pragmatic, low-overhead harvesting layer focused on rapid warmstarts and guarded exploration that works across diverse GPUs and sequence-length mixes.

Deliverables: harvester daemon (C++ runtime shim + control-plane ingest), microprobe harness, warmstart store interface, selection policy integration, dashboards, and canary rollout automation.
updates: 2025-02-10: Ticket created after spike investigating repeated decode tail spikes on m40 and a100 mixed pools. Initial proposal drafted.

2025-02-14: Architecture review with serving runtime and infra. Decided to keep probes lightweight (max 2 probes / 10k requests) and to record only aggregated metrics to control plane to limit cardinality.

2025-02-20: Prototype microprobe harness implemented. Ran local microbench across p4, a100, and t4 nodes. Observed candidate kernels with utility improvements up to 18% for long-prefill sequences, and 9% for mixed decode workloads.
2025-02-27: Design review feedback from PM (Ilya Novak) — add explicit prefill/decode split and persistent fallback marker. Added rollback cooldown requirement in design.
2025-03-01: Integration spike with KV cache subsystem. Confirmed probes must simulate realistic KV cache usage to avoid misleading results. Adjusted probe workload generator.
2025-03-04: Blocking: test harness for cross-node warmstart push is immature. Dependency opened (ENG-260002). Scheduled pairing with infra team next week.
2025-03-05: Started implementing warmstart LRU store and confidence decay. Canary plan drafted.
acceptance_criteria: Canary: rolled out to a subset of nodes (10%) for 48h with automatic rollback triggers configured.
Median end-to-end latency for decode workloads does not regress; 99p latency improves by at least 4% for at least one representative long-sequence model (GPT-like) in canary.
Warmstart mapping covers >= 60% of incoming signatures in the canary pool after 48h with >= 85% selection agreement vs offline oracle.
Probing overhead <= 0.05% of total requests in steady state and never exceeds 0.5% during exploration windows.
Automated rollback and blacklist logic works (simulated failure test) and entries respect cooldown windows.
testing_plan: Unit tests for signature creation and LRU store behavior.
Microbench suite across p4, t4, a100 for representative kernels and sequence-length buckets (8, 64, 256, 1024).
End-to-end canary with A/B comparison against baseline kernel-picker measuring latency, tokens/sec, and cost per 1M tokens.
Chaos test: inject delayed probe metrics and corrupted probe results to verify safety guards.
Regression set: run on previously failing workloads (customer traces anonymized) to ensure no regression.
Dashboard smoke tests: ensure coverage, probe-rate, and warmstart-accuracy panels populate.
notes: Consider future integration with Optimize recommendations to seed initial mapping for new clusters.
Long-term: evaluate replacing bandit-lite with small multi-armed bandit library if probe budgets prove too conservative.
Follow-up ticket suggested to export warmstart artifact for Private deployments to speed cold starts in VPC customers.
